Therefore, despite models improving it remains vital to keep a human in the loop to ensure a geolocation is precise and correct.

While many models were good at identifying general areas, pinpointing exact coordinates was more of a challenge. As any online investigator knows, this final stretch in identifying an exact spot is vitally important. Our tests show that human geolocators still have the edge in this area.
But the tests also showed why humans remain necessary for accurate and trustworthy geolocation work, as no models were foolproof.

The results showed that the current generation of models have improved geolocation capabilities. Anthropic’s Opus and Fable, as well as Google’s recent Gemini 4 Argon model, performed the best on geolocations, narrowing down locations from images faster than a human could under specific conditions.

In September, the AI company Anthropic claimed its models were approaching “superhuman capabilities for geolocating outdoor photos”. Bellingcat put that claim to the test by benchmarking the performance of Anthropic and other LLMs. Here’s what we found: www.bellingcat.com/resources/20...
